name: Multi-PR Stacking-Order Planner
description: Determine the real merge order of N open PRs by measuring what actually conflicts. mergeStateStatus CLEAN is evaluated in ISOLATION and says nothing about PR-to-PR overlap: seven CLEAN PRs looked mutually conflicting and were fully stackable because the overlapping content was BYTE-IDENTICAL, so whichever merged second was a no-op. Conflict COST is measured with a throwaway merge and counted in unmerged paths, never estimated from diff size - a +72k-line PR measured a five-file conflict surface.

prs.description: PR refs to order. One PR has no ordering problem.

base_ref.description: The base to measure against, e.g. origin/main

probe_branch_prefix.description: Every merge probe runs on a THROWAWAY branch; a probe that dirties a real branch is a process failure

forge_token.description: Reference NAME of the forge credential the gh calls authenticate with. This blueprint is the only one in its range that talks to a forge, so it is the only one that must declare a credential. Declaring it as a secret_ref (rather than leaving it implicit in the ambient environment) is what makes the export-redaction rule checkable: the VALUE may never enter an artifact, a log, an export bundle or a replay journal - only this reference name travels. The workflow never reads, prints or rotates the credential.

measurer.description: Runs git plumbing only: changed-file lists, byte digests, throwaway merges, revision walks

semantic_judge.description: Judges only the residue byte-identity cannot settle: two different edits that mean the same thing, or the reverse

stages.title: S0 LIST changed files per PR, three-dot against the base

work_unit.title: List each PR's changed files with a three-dot diff
work_unit.question_or_target: For each PR compute the changed-file set using base...head, so working-tree noise is excluded.
work_unit.evidence_requirement: records the exact three-dot diff command per PR alongside its file list
tests_required: a two-dot diff must be rejected: it folds in working-tree noise, which is how an untracked file appears to be 'in the PR'
a stale branch far behind the base must be measured with three dots, or it appears to propose mass deletion
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: none - the recorded command is the evidence
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BP3-PLN03-S0 only when every PR carries a three-dot command string and a file list; otherwise FAILED:BP3-PLN03-S0 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to fetching the base first

stages.title: S1 PAIRWISE overlap matrix (shared exact primitive)
S2 TEST byte-identity of the overlapping content

work_unit.title: Digest the overlapping content on both sides of every overlapping pair
work_unit.question_or_target: For each overlapping path in each pair, compare content digests; byte-identical overlap is stackable, not conflicting.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a digest comparison is exact; an LLM opinion on sameness is not

work_unit.evidence_requirement: each overlapping path records both digests, so the identical/conflicting split is recomputable
tests_required: two PRs whose overlapping content is byte-identical must be reported STACKABLE, not conflicting
content read for digesting must come from the committed blob, never from the working tree, because line endings differ between them on this platform
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the semantic judge only for pairs that differ but may mean the same thing
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BP3-PLN03-S2 only when every overlapping path carries two digests and an identical/conflicting verdict; otherwise FAILED:BP3-PLN03-S2 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to a per-hunk comparison

stages.title: S3 MEASURE the real conflict surface with a throwaway merge

work_unit.title: Count unmerged paths from a throwaway merge, then abort it
work_unit.question_or_target: On a throwaway branch, merge without committing and count the unmerged paths; that count, not the diff size, is the cost.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the conflict surface must be measured, because line count is not a cost proxy

work_unit.evidence_requirement: records the probe branch name, the unmerged-path count, and the abort that followed
tests_required: every probe must run on a throwaway branch and must be aborted; a probe that leaves the tree dirty is a process failure
a large-diff PR with a small conflict surface must report the SMALL number - the whole point is that line count misleads
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: none - the recorded branch and counts are the evidence
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BP3-PLN03-S3 only when every probe branch was created, counted, and aborted, and the working tree is clean; otherwise FAILED:BP3-PLN03-S3 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to a fresh throwaway branch

stages.title: S3 gate: every probe branch aborted, working tree clean
S4 DETECT superset relations - if B contains A, reconcile from B

work_unit.title: Find pairs where one PR already contains the other's work
work_unit.question_or_target: For each ordered pair, decide whether B contains A by walking revisions; if so, close A in B's favour.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a revision-set containment test is exact

work_unit.evidence_requirement: each superset claim records the two revision sets that establish containment
tests_required: a PR whose commits are all present in another must be reported as superseded, not as a separate merge
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the semantic judge when containment holds by revision but the diffs differ
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BP3-PLN03-S4 only when every superset claim records both revision sets; otherwise FAILED:BP3-PLN03-S4 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to a diff-level containment check

stages.title: S5 EMIT the merge order, ranked by measured surface

work_unit.title: Emit the recommended merge order
work_unit.question_or_target: Order the PRs by measured conflict surface ascending, with deterministic tie-breaks, and list the byte-identical stackable pairs.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the ordering rule is declared and arithmetic, so two runs agree

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the order records, per PR, the surface count that placed it and any superset relation that removed it
tests_required: the order must be stable across two runs on the same inputs
a superseded PR must not appear in the order at all
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BP3-PLN03-S5 only when every ordered PR carries the surface count that placed it; otherwise FAILED:BP3-PLN03-S5 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: none; a deterministic ordering that fails is a defect

stages.title: S5 gate: the order came from measurement, not from mergeStateStatus or line count
S5 gate: cost was counted in unmerged paths, not estimated from diff size

impact.blast_radius: all probing happens on throwaway branches which are aborted; the real branches are read-only and only command-center/stacking/** is written

x_extensions.distinguishing_mechanism: MERGE ORDERING over MEASURED git refs, decided by byte-identity of the overlapping content plus a throwaway-merge unmerged-path count plus revision-set containment. It shares the overlap primitive with BP-PLN-02 by REFERENCE; the decision, the inputs and the deciding tests are all different. BP-REL-01 shepherds ONE PR; this orders many before any is shepherded.
x_extensions.honest_bound: byte-identity is a strong but incomplete conflict predictor: two textually different edits can still conflict semantically, which is why a semantic judge exists for exactly that residue and nothing else.

worked_example.name: byte-identical overlap is stackable, and surface beats line count
worked_example.narrative: PR-1 and PR-2 both change ci.yml. The bytes they land there are IDENTICAL (PR-2 already contains PR-1's edit), so the pair is STACKABLE and whichever merges second is a no-op on that path. PR-3 also touches ci.yml but with different bytes, so PR-1/PR-3 is a true conflict. Ordering then runs on the measured surface: PR-3 has the largest diff but only one conflicting path, so it is not automatically last.

controls.mutate: change pr2's ci.yml bytes to 'on: schedule'
controls.why: the digest comparison is doing the work - identical bytes are what make the pair stackable, not the shared path
